items.explanation: The Senate's League rejection, the 1920s immigration quotas, and the Red Scare all point toward withdrawal — but a truly isolationist nation would not keep ruling the Philippines, Guam, and Puerto Rico. The empire is the strongest counter-evidence.
items.fact_source: u7.md §The story — the 1898 empire: "holding the Philippines, Guam, and Puerto Rico"; the Senate rejected League membership and "the country turned inward"; immigration quotas of 1921 and 1924

option_explanations.A: Incorrect. The Senate's rejection of the League supports the isolationist description; it does not challenge it.
option_explanations.B: Incorrect. The immigration quotas were part of the inward, nativist turn; they support the description.
option_explanations.C: Correct. Continuing to rule an overseas empire contradicts the claim of pure isolationism.
option_explanations.D: Incorrect. The Red Scare was part of the postwar inward panic; it supports the description.

options: (A) The Senate rejected membership in the League of Nations, refusing any American commitment to collective security
(B) Congress passed immigration quotas aimed at southern and eastern Europeans and Asians
(C) The United States continued to hold the Philippines, Guam, and Puerto Rico, the overseas empire won in 1898
(D) The Red Scare of 1919–1920 targeted suspected communists and anarchists
items.stem: A historian describes the United States of the 1920s as purely isolationist. Which of the following presents the strongest challenge to that description?

items.explanation: American banks lent heavily to Britain and France and American factories sold them war goods. Those ties meant the United States was never a disinterested bystander, and they pulled American policy toward the Allies.
items.fact_source: u7.md §What the exam tests here — "WWI entry rested on submarine warfare, the Zimmermann telegram, and economic ties to the Allies"

option_explanations.A: Incorrect. The United States traded heavily with Europe; it was not cut off from European commerce.
option_explanations.B: Correct. Extensive American trade and loans with Britain and France made genuine neutrality difficult to sustain.
option_explanations.C: Incorrect. American economic ties were to the Allies, not to Germany.
option_explanations.D: Incorrect. The Allies did not pay the United States to enter the war.

options: (A) The United States had no trade with any European country before 1917
(B) Extensive American trade and loans with Britain and France made genuine neutrality difficult to sustain
(C) Germany was America's largest trading partner, and the United States wanted to protect that profitable trade
(D) The Allies paid the United States to enter the war
items.stem: In explaining why the United States entered World War I, historians cite German submarine warfare and the Zimmermann telegram — and also American economic ties to the Allies. Those economic ties mattered because...

items.explanation: Cut off from British goods first by Jefferson's embargo and then by war, Americans built their own factories — and having survived a second war with Britain, they felt a new national pride. Industry and nationalism grew together.
items.fact_source: u4.md §The story — "his 1807 Embargo Act, meant to punish Britain and France, cut Americans off from British manufactured goods and forced them to make their own. The War of 1812 did the same thing more dramatically. When the war ended, a wave of national pride and new factories produced what Americans called the Market Revolution"

option_explanations.A: Incorrect. The United States did not conquer Canada in the War of 1812.
option_explanations.B: Incorrect. The war accelerated the Market Revolution; it did not end it.
option_explanations.C: Incorrect. Trade with Britain resumed after the war.
option_explanations.D: Correct. The cutoff from British goods forced domestic manufacturing, and surviving the war fed national pride.

options: (A) The United States decisively conquered Canada and seized British colonies
(B) The war ended the Market Revolution and restored subsistence farming as the foundation of the entire American economy for decades
(C) Britain agreed to abandon all trade with the United States permanently
(D) Cut off from British goods, Americans built their own factories — and surviving a second war with Britain fed national pride
items.stem: The War of 1812 ended in stalemate, yet it fueled American nationalism and domestic industry. Which of the following best explains why a stalemated war had these effects?

items.explanation: The print shows an official, large-scale public celebration — evidence that contemporaries saw the canal as a proud collective achievement, the kind of internal improvement that tied the young nation together.
items.fact_source: u4.md §The story — canals like the Erie (1825) "tied distant regions into one commercial web"; §Key terms — Erie Canal: "Waterway linking the Great Lakes to New York City; made New York the commercial capital"

option_explanations.A: Correct. The official celebration shows Americans treating the canal as a proud national achievement that tied the country together.
option_explanations.B: Incorrect. The canal served American commerce; British merchants did not control it.
option_explanations.C: Incorrect. The canal made New York the commercial capital; New Yorkers celebrated it rather than opposing it.
option_explanations.D: Incorrect. Canal-building continued as part of the Market Revolution; the celebration did not mark its end.

options: (A) Americans treated internal improvements like the canal as proud national achievements that tied the country together
(B) The canal was celebrated mainly by British merchants who controlled American trade
(C) New Yorkers opposed the canal because it threatened the city's commerce
(D) The celebration marked the end of all canal-building in the United States, since railroads had already replaced water transport
items.stem: The image shows New York's official celebration of the Erie Canal's opening in 1825. The scale and official character of the celebration best support which of the following conclusions?

items.explanation: The engraving shows a vast, orderly factory complex — visual evidence that Lowell concentrated production on an industrial scale, reorganizing both work and daily life for the young women who tended the looms.
items.fact_source: u4.md §The story — "In Lowell, Massachusetts, young women left farms to tend power looms for cash wages — a brand-new way of life"

option_explanations.A: Incorrect. Lowell employed young farm women for cash wages; enslaved labor powered Southern cotton agriculture.
option_explanations.B: Incorrect. The Lowell mills were a private enterprise, not a federal project.
option_explanations.C: Correct. The image shows large-scale, planned factory production — a new way of organizing work and life.
option_explanations.D: Incorrect. The Lowell women left their family farms to work in the mills.

options: (A) The Lowell mills relied on enslaved labor to tend the power looms
(B) The federal government built and operated the Lowell mills
(C) The Lowell system concentrated production in large, planned factory complexes — a new way of organizing work and daily life
(D) The Lowell system kept young women working within their family farm households in the countryside instead of moving to the new mill towns
items.stem: A historian could best use this image of the Boott Cotton Mills as evidence for which of the following claims about the Lowell system?

items.explanation: The Awakening's perfectionist message — that society could be improved — pushed thousands of converts into organized reform: temperance, public schools, care for the mentally ill, and above all abolition.
items.fact_source: u4.md §The story — "a religious revival, the Second Great Awakening, convinced thousands of Americans that society itself could be perfected. Reformers launched crusades against alcohol, for public schools..., and — most explosively — against slavery"

option_explanations.A: Incorrect. No national church was established in the United States.
option_explanations.B: Incorrect. Religious disagreement among Protestants continued.
option_explanations.C: Incorrect. The Awakening taught the opposite — that reform of society was both possible and urgent.
option_explanations.D: Correct. The Awakening's perfectionism inspired the era's reform crusades.

options: (A) Establishing a single national church for the United States
(B) Ending all religious disagreement among Protestants
(C) Persuading Americans that reform of society was impossible and that human nature could never truly be improved
(D) Convincing thousands of Americans that society itself could be perfected, inspiring reform crusades
items.stem: The Second Great Awakening shaped American culture in the 1820s and 1830s primarily by...

items.explanation: Borrowing the Declaration's language was a deliberate strategy: if 'all men are created equal' was America's founding truth, then women could claim it too.
items.fact_source: u4.md §The story — the Seneca Falls Convention (1848) issued a "Declaration of Sentiments modeled on the Declaration of Independence"

option_explanations.A: Incorrect. Independence from Britain had been declared in 1776, seventy years earlier.
option_explanations.B: Correct. The reformers claimed the founding generation's ideals of liberty and equality for women.
option_explanations.C: Incorrect. The reformers opposed slavery; many were abolitionists themselves.
option_explanations.D: Incorrect. No new constitutional convention was called at Seneca Falls.

options: (A) Declaring a new independence from the British Empire, just as the founders had done in 1776
(B) Claiming the founding generation's ideals of liberty and equality for women
(C) Endorsing the expansion of slavery into new territories
(D) Calling for a new constitutional convention
items.stem: "In 1848, at Seneca Falls, New York, Elizabeth Cady Stanton and Lucretia Mott held the first women's-rights convention and issued a Declaration of Sentiments modeled on the Declaration of Independence." By modeling their Declaration of Sentiments on the Declaration of Independence, the Seneca Falls reformers were most directly...

stimulus.text: In 1848, at Seneca Falls, New York, Elizabeth Cady Stanton and Lucretia Mott held the first women's-rights convention and issued a Declaration of Sentiments modeled on the Declaration of Independence.

items.explanation: The Market Revolution replaced local, household-based production with commercial farming, wage work, and markets linked by canals, steamboats, and railroads.
items.fact_source: u4.md §Key terms — Market Revolution: "The shift to commercial agriculture, wage labor, and regionally linked markets via canals, steamboats, and rail"

option_explanations.A: Correct. Commercial agriculture, wage labor, and linked markets replaced subsistence farming and household production.
option_explanations.B: Incorrect. The Market Revolution expanded trade; it did not end it.
option_explanations.C: Incorrect. The pattern was reversed: the North moved toward wage labor while the South deepened slavery.
option_explanations.D: Incorrect. Canals, steamboats, and railroads tied regions into one commercial web; they did not isolate them.

options: (A) Commercial agriculture, wage labor, and linked markets replaced subsistence farming and household production
(B) Americans abandoned all forms of trade and returned to self-sufficient farms, isolated from national markets and from each other
(C) The South moved toward wage labor while the North deepened its commitment to slavery
(D) Canals, steamboats, and railroads isolated each region from the others
items.stem: Which of the following best describes the Market Revolution's effect on how ordinary Americans lived and worked?

items.explanation: Jefferson intended the embargo as a foreign-policy weapon against Britain and France. Its most lasting effect was domestic and unintended: cut off from British goods, Americans built their own factories.
items.fact_source: u4.md §The story — "Jefferson's own policies helped trigger it against his intentions: his 1807 Embargo Act, meant to punish Britain and France, cut Americans off from British manufactured goods and forced them to make their own"

option_explanations.A: Incorrect. The act backfired economically; it did not force Britain to change course.
option_explanations.B: Correct. The embargo's lasting consequence — domestic manufacturing growth — was the opposite of its intended foreign-policy purpose.
option_explanations.C: Incorrect. The manufacturing growth was unintended; Jefferson did not design the embargo as an industrial program.
option_explanations.D: Incorrect. The Louisiana Purchase, not the Embargo Act, was the treaty with France.

options: (A) A successful use of economic pressure that forced Britain to change its policies toward American trade
(B) A foreign-policy measure whose unintended result was the growth of American manufacturing
(C) A domestic manufacturing program that Jefferson designed to industrialize the nation
(D) A treaty with France that doubled the nation's territory
items.stem: Historians note that Jefferson's Embargo Act helped trigger the Market Revolution "against his intentions." The Embargo Act is therefore best used as an example of which of the following?

items.explanation: The domestic ideal told respectable women to stay home, yet the 1840s also produced the first women's-rights convention — the ideal shaped most women's lives while a minority of activists publicly challenged it.
items.fact_source: u4.md §Key terms — Cult of domesticity: "Ideal that respectable women belonged in the home, shaping middle-class gender roles amid women's growing public activism"; §The story — Seneca Falls Convention (1848)

option_explanations.A: Incorrect. The ideal held that politics was not women's sphere.
option_explanations.B: Incorrect. The Seneca Falls reformers challenged the ideal rather than endorsing it.
option_explanations.C: Correct. The ideal constrained most middle-class women even as activists entered public reform.
option_explanations.D: Incorrect. No federal ban on women attending reform conventions existed.

options: (A) All American women agreed that politics was properly their sphere and entered public life without opposition
(B) The Seneca Falls reformers endorsed the cult of domesticity
(C) The ideal constrained most middle-class women's lives even as a minority of activists entered public reform
(D) The federal government banned women from attending reform conventions
items.stem: The "cult of domesticity" — the ideal that respectable women belonged in the home — coexisted in the 1840s with the Seneca Falls Convention because...
